name: Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa)
ecoregions: North Ryukyu Islands, Japan|South Ryukyu Islands, Japan
note: The reference locale: the cue table is Okinawa's own sun, moon and temperature.

name: Great Barrier Reef
ecoregions: Central and northern Great Barrier Reef|Southern Great Barrier Reef (including Keppel Islands and Capricorn Bunker Reefs)
note: Southern hemisphere: seasons are moved onto the Okinawa calendar by the 182.6 day flip. The SeaSim tank runs a programmed 6-month-offset Davies profile, so it has no events of its own on the graph.

name: Subtropical eastern Australia
note: Solitary Islands animals; the one record is an anemone with no year, so it has no moon age and is not on the graph.

name: Western Australia, autumn season
ecoregions: Houtman Abrolhos Islands, west Australia|Ningaloo Reef and coastal north-west Australia|Scott Reef, west Australia
note: March-April mass spawning at Scott Reef, Ningaloo and the Abrolhos (Foster et al. 2018; Gilmour et al. 2016). Spring split off as wa_spring.

name: Western Australia, spring season
ecoregions: Houtman Abrolhos Islands, west Australia|Ningaloo Reef and coastal north-west Australia|Scott Reef, west Australia
note: Scott Reef's smaller October-November spawning (Foster et al. 2018, observed nights only; the 18 dates inferred from egg colour are left out). Outline only.

name: Taiwan and coastal China
note: No cue site yet.

name: Singapore and the Sunda Shelf
ecoregions: Strait of Malacca, eastern Sumatra and Singapore|Sunda Shelf, south-east Asia|Java Sea, Indonesia|West Sumatra, Indonesia
note: Within 10 degrees of the equator, so the season axis is left unaligned.

name: Philippines and Wallacea
ecoregions: North Philippines|Sulu Sea, Philippines|Makassar Strait, Indonesia
note: Coral Triangle edge. Season axis unaligned for the equatorial sites.

name: Gulf of Thailand, east (Rayong, Chonburi)
note: Night spawners, peak early March (Mehrotra et al. 2026 S1 Table). Daytime Pavona (Oct-Nov, around full moon) is a different cue and is left out.

name: Gulf of Thailand, west (Koh Tao, Koh Phangan)
note: Night spawners, peak early April (Mehrotra et al. 2026 S1 Table). Daytime Pavona left out.

name: Melanesia (Fiji, Solomons, New Guinea)
ecoregions: Fiji|Solomon Islands and Bougainville|Bismarck Sea, Papua New Guinea
note: Equatorial Solomons site is unaligned; Fiji is 18 S.

name: Eastern Pacific
ecoregions: Galapagos Islands|Costa Rica and Panama, Pacific coast
note: A Pavona window, not a community one: 18 of 20 nights are Uva Island, Panama (Glynn et al. 2000). No clock window: the three Pavona species spawn at different times of day.

name: Flower Garden Banks (Gulf of Mexico)
note: Orbicella, Pseudodiploria and Stephanocoenia, August, 7 to 9 days after full (Vize et al. 2005). In situ water record exists: NDBC 42047 (NCEI 0306554).

name: Caribbean reef tract (Florida Keys, Belize, Panama, Curacao)
note: Acropora and Dendrogyra, July-September, 2 to 5 days after full. Reference fixed at the Upper Florida Keys (records from Williams et al. 2023; NDBC MLRF1 nearby): the median of the sites falls in the open Gulf.

name: Gulf of Aqaba (Eilat)
note: Northern tip of the Red Sea, 29.5 N. Rich but broad: species spawn on their own moon phases (Shlesinger & Loya 1985) and two dominant species lost lunar synchrony after 2015 (Shlesinger & Loya 2019). Use the species rows.

name: Northern Red Sea (Hurghada, NEOM)
note: Placeholder, no dated records in the repo yet. Acropora spawn late April to May here, later than Thuwal (Osman et al. 2024, supplementary Table S1 not yet extracted).

name: Central Red Sea (Thuwal, Saudi Arabia)
ecoregions: North and central Red Sea|Red Sea (central)
note: Thuwal reefs, 22 N. Acropora first, at the April full moon, then other families into June (Bouwmeester et al. 2015, 2016).

name: Arabian (Persian) Gulf
ecoregions: Arabian/Persian Gulf|North and central Red Sea
note: Takes the Tarut Bay row the database files under the Red Sea ecoregion (lon 50.1). In situ nights only: the UAE ex situ rows stay out, and Al Aqah is on the Gulf of Oman coast.

name: Maldives, October to December season
note: Baa and North Male atolls, 4-5 N. The first of two Acropora seasons a year (Monfared et al. 2023). Same sky as maldives_mar_apr.

name: Maldives, March to April season
note: Baa and North Male atolls, 4-5 N. The second Acropora season, larger and tighter (Monfared et al. 2023).

name: Reunion (Mascarene Islands)
note: 21 S. Acropora muricata Oct-Nov, faviids Jan-Feb; one unpublished source (Hoarau). Start times fall before sunset: check the clock.

name: Kenya, Tanzania and Madagascar
ecoregions: Kenya and Tanzania coast|West and south Madagascar
note: Thin outline: five nights from three sources, 4 to 22 S. Includes daytime Porites rus at Zanzibar.

name: Chagos Archipelago
note: One night (daytime Fungia danai, Mangubhai et al. 2007). Outline only.

name: Gulf of Mannar (south-east India)
ecoregions: North Sri Lanka, Gulf of Mannar and east India
note: Four March nights, Tuticorin Acropora (Raj & Edward 2010). Outline only.

name: Hawaii
note: Two clusters: Pocillopora meandrina at Molokini in April-May near full moon, Montipora in Kaneohe Bay in June-July. Use the species rows for a target.

name: French Polynesia (Moorea)
note: Moorea Acropora, October-November, 5 to 12 days after full (Carroll et al. 2006).

name: American Samoa
note: Faga'alu Porites and others, November, 3 to 5 days after full (Itano & Buckley 1988; Mundy & Green 1999). Outline only.

name: Temperate Japan (Shikoku, Kyushu)
note: Not split: both ecoregions are broad on the moon on their own. Season is tight (July-August); the lunar spread is real at 32-33 N (Mezaki et al. 2007, 2006 especially). Ready only through the faviid species rows (Platygyra, Favites, 6-10 days after full).

name: Palau, February to June season
note: 7 N. The main multispecies season, April-May (Penland et al. 2004; Gouezo et al. 2020). Needs the ex situ rows: only 4 in situ nights.

name: Palau, July to January season
note: The second, smaller season around the September equinox (Penland et al. 2004): Montipora and Acropora, 2002 only. Outline only.

name: Marianas (Guam, Saipan)
note: Guam Acropora in July-August, all held ex situ (Kenyon 1994). Saipan is a calendar-same site at low confidence (one social-media anemone record).
